figures.caption: Exploration of the mechanism of action of Peptide 4 using molecular dynamics simulations. A) The alterations in the relative positions of the first residue (R1), central hydrophobic residues, and the last residue (R11) of Peptide 4 in relation to the surface of POPG membrane during a 300 ns AA MD simulation. The binding energy of Peptide 4 with the membrane was calculated to be −74.19 kcal mol−1; B) AA MD simulation revealed a three-step mechanism of Peptide 4 action on the POPG membrane: initial binding of Peptide 4 to the membrane surface, complete membrane penetration, and alternating helical and unfolded conformations of the peptide's hydrophilic tail (left). The depression of POPG membrane induced by the action of Peptide 4 (right). C) CG US simulations showed that the membrane breakage occurred when one Peptide 4 crossed the membrane for the 14th and 13th times at rates of 0.1 and 0.5 nm ns−1, respectively. Additionally, membrane breakage was observed when two peptides crossed the membrane for the 6th and 3rd times, respectively, at rates of 0.1 and 0.5 nm ns−1 (left). The PMF of Peptide 4 during translocation through the membrane was plotted against the corresponding times (right). D) Size and duration of the water pores formed as Peptide 4 crosses the POPG membrane. POPG: 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphatidylglycerol; AA MD: all-atom molecular dynamics; CG US: coarse-grained umbrella sampling; PMF: potential of mean force.
